idiom_name: protocol composition for components; GameplayKit GKEntity/GKComponent on Apple platforms
implementation_notes: Swift's composition unit is the protocol: a component conforms to a narrow protocol (or is a value type conforming to one), the entity holds [any Component] and updates by iterating, and protocol composition types (Physics & Renderable) let one parameter require several capabilities without declaring a new protocol (docs.swift.org). On Apple platforms GameplayKit supplies the roles directly - GKEntity is documented as an object whose functionality is 'entirely provided by a collection of component objects', GKComponent is the subclassable base, GKComponentSystem drives per-component-type updates in a deterministic order - so use it where the runtime is available and you want the framework's lifecycle instead of your own loop.
pitfalls: Value-type components are copied with the entity: mutating part inside a for-in loop mutates a copy unless the container is mutating and iterates indices, so state changes can be silently dropped.
A protocol with Self or associated-type requirements cannot be used as any Component, so a component protocol must stay fully existential to live in an array of parts.
GameplayKit's GKComponent is a class holding an entity back-reference; keeping a strong reference from component to entity creates a retain cycle unless the component is removed on teardown.

variants.name: GameplayKit GKEntity with GKComponent subclasses
variants.implementation_notes: GameplayKit provides the container, the component base class and two dispatch modes: per-entity (call GKEntity.update(deltaTime:) and let it forward to its components) or per-component-type (a GKComponentSystem owns every component of one class and forwards update(deltaTime:) to them in a controlled order). Use the per-component mode once update order matters, and remember that components get an entity back-reference from the framework.
pitfalls: GKComponent holds an entity back-reference; a component that also strongly references game objects can keep the whole graph alive after removal.
GKComponent subclasses are classes with a no-argument initialiser contract - configuration has to happen after construction or through the entity.
GameplayKit is Apple-platform only, so code sharing with server-side Swift needs the protocol-composition variant behind a boundary.
